title: The explorer does not automatically refresh when underlying data changes
body:
Reported by hv on 2026-09-23, in hv's words to vc: "I also just found a refresh bug with the Explorer. The data in the app doesn't refresh when the underlying data changes."

Ruling (hv, 2026-09-23, in the same session): "It either needs to do the refresh automatically or we need a refresh key. I'd prefer it to be automatic, but will settle for a key (or a slash-refresh command if needed)." Fix it asap. It is a 3.2.1 item.

Routing (vc, on hv's word): ic, because the explorer (`intent explore`) is ic's surface; cc joins if the cause is in intentd's change feed. ic records the reproduction and names the mechanism here before building, and says which of the three shapes it builds and why: automatic refresh first, then a key or a `/refresh` command only if automatic cannot be done soundly.


Reproduced (ic, 2026-09-23, 07:42Z to 07:49Z by date -u): the installed pair 099088acd, `intent explore` driven in a 120x32 pty rendered by pyte, on a scratch project under an isolated HOME (one thread, one issue), with a second process writing through the CLI.

1. The issues list is open. A second process runs `intent issues add`. Four seconds later the list has not changed, a Down arrow does not change it, and the omnibox finds no `0002`. Backspace to the threads list and back to the issues list still shows only `0001`.
2. The explorer's own palette runs `/issues add PaletteProbe`. It prints `created: ... 0003` and the info row says `ok`, yet the list the explorer re-reads straight afterwards shows `0001` and `0002` only. A new `intent explore` shows all three.
3. Issue 0001 is open and a second process changes its title. The explorer still shows the old title, and a severity edit made in it is refused: `issue 0001 changed while this command was running -- nothing was written`. The store keeps the second process's title, so nothing is lost.
4. The same edit three seconds later is refused again. An entity another writer has touched cannot be edited from that explorer until it is restarted.

Mechanism, read in the source and matching all four drives:

- `Facade::open` loads the whole canon into memory (`ingest::load_fresh`), and every read the explorer makes (`st_list`, `issue_list`, `rows_for`, `entity_json`) answers from that copy. The copy moves only for that facade's own writes and syncs. The explorer holds one facade for its whole session (`render.rs`, `explore_here`: `Live { facade: open()? }`), so no commit by another connection ever reaches it: not a CLI write from another terminal or node, not intentd's ingest of a hand edit, and not the explorer's own `/` commands, which `render::run` runs through a second facade. That is why re-entering a view, and the unconditional re-read after a `/` command (`tui/run.rs`, `Step::Run`), both paint the model as it stood at launch. `intent mcp` met the same class and opens a facade per request for exactly this reason (`mcp_stdio.rs`, "OPEN PER REQUEST"). The explorer is the long-lived holder that was left.
- The loop blocks on `event::read()` (`tui/run.rs`) and re-reads rows only when the view changes or after its own acts, and the omnibox's entities are read once at launch. So with only the facade fixed, a change would still show only after a key moved the view.
- The refused edit is `Store::commit_mutation`'s compare-and-swap judging the write against the stale snapshot. It is correct, it is why nothing was lost, and it repeats because the snapshot never moves.
- Not the cause: intentd's change feed. The explorer never talks to intentd. intentd's own facade is also long-lived and catches up through its ingest of the canon files each write leaves on disk; that was not measured here. The web face was not measured either: it fetches each request from intentd and is not the explorer.

Shape (ic, sent to vc before any code): AUTOMATIC, and sound with no daemon running.

1. `Facade::catch_up`: when this connection's `PRAGMA data_version` has moved since the canon was last loaded, reload the canon through the door `open` uses (`ingest::load_fresh`) and say so. `Store::data_version` exists for issue 0441: it moves when another connection commits and never for this one's own writes, so no writer has to remember anything. When nothing moved it costs one pragma read. Measured on this estate's live store: a warm open, load and list (`intent outs`) takes about 0.13s end to end, and `data_version` also moves on commits that carry no model change (a heartbeat was followed by two more commits with no event), so a reload can run with nothing new to show, at that cost.
2. The explorer's source catches up before every read: rows, the omnibox index, and the value an edit starts from. It never catches up before a write, so the compare-and-swap still judges an edit against the record it started from, and a refused edit shows the current record on the next pass.
3. The loop waits for a key with a timeout instead of blocking. On a pass with no key, no edit open and the terminal not lent, it asks whether the store moved. If it did, the loop re-reads the current view and the omnibox index, and keeps the cursor on the same row by name rather than by position, because a new issue or thread sorts above the rows already listed. The index is not re-read while a query is typed, so the dropdown does not move under the pick. The search pane is not re-run on a tick: its answer comes from a query that reconciles and writes the index, and its freshness line (AC-21.1) says how current it is. It re-runs when entered, as now.
4. No refresh key and no `/refresh` command: automatic is sound, and hv preferred it.

Proof: pure arms in `tui::` for the cursor following its row by name and for when a refresh may run; an intentsvcs arm for `catch_up` (a second connection commits and the reads show it; nothing moved is a no-op; the facade's own write does not count); and the four drives above repeated on the built binary, each showing the change without a key.

Built (ic, 2026-09-23), the automatic shape above, accepted by vc: `Facade::catch_up`; the explorer's source catches up before every read and never before a write; and the loop waits 500ms for a key and, on an idle pass with no edit open, re-reads the view when the store moved. Driven in a pty on the built debug pair (tmp/wt-ic-0520 at c419e8719) against scratch projects, with no key pressed after any change:

1. The issues list shows an outside `intent issues add` within 1.5s, and the omnibox finds the new id. The cursor stays on its row by name: the counter went from `2/2` to `3/3` on `0001`, where keeping the position would read `2/3`.
2. The explorer's own `/issues add` shows on the return from the command.
3. An outside title change shows within 1.5s, and a severity edit made after it is saved; the store holds both.
4. With no daemon, a hand edit of an issue's canon file does not show after 4s, and shows within 1.5s of `intent sync --to-store`. Under a scratch intentd watching the project, it shows within 6s with no sync.
5. Idle cost, on a scratch model of 400 issues and 40 threads: 60s idle with nothing committed cost the explorer 0.01s of CPU, which is ps's resolution. The next 60s, with an outside commit every 3s (20 commits), cost 0.12s. So a reload is visible to the instrument, at about 5.5ms each, and the idle ticks made none.

Limit, declared rather than built (ic, accepted by vc on 2026-09-23): THE EXPLORER FOLLOWS THE STORE. A file edited by hand under `intent/` reaches it when something commits that edit to the store: intentd's ingest where a daemon watches the project, and `intent sync --to-store` where none does (drive 4). No idle pass reads the disk, for three reasons. It would be a second ingester beside intentd. It would be work on every idle tick. And it is the limit every CLI verb already has, under hv's ruling of 2026-08-14 that the daily driver does not read the files (`ingest::load_fresh`).

**LANDED, NOT DEPLOYED (ic, 2026-09-23, on vc's word).** At 89015b037 on 987268553, from refs/bank/ic/0520/on-987268553 (blob 5933ef69e). The patch-id was read back from the applied tree before the commit and again from the landed commit, 637bede65 both times: the id judged as refs/bank/ic/0520/judged-c419e8719 (blob c8a0c7c39). The pre-commit gate passed on every arm.

**THE JUDGING.** ic's run on c419e8719, above. Then cc's train run on 987268553 with 0520, 0524 and 0523 stage 1, running CI's rust lines: fmt, both clippy lines, the doc step and the workspace test. Nothing red was 0520's, and cc's re-run with 0523 stage 1 v2 was green throughout.

**DEPLOYMENT.** `native/rust/` deploys on neither save nor commit (0518). The explorer on this machine refreshes from hv's next `bin/devbin build all`. Until then the gate's currency line reads REFUSING and a push is refused (decision 30).
